title: Sustained Batch Fairness Orchestrator (SBO): SLO-aware scheduler for continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Continuous batching improves throughput but creates complex resource contention between latency-sensitive tenants and heavy batch workloads. Current preemption logic is brittle under mixed workloads: it either kills large batches (hurting throughput) or delays small interactive requests (breaking p95 SLOs). We need an orchestrator that enforces SLOs while preserving overall GPU efficiency and KV cache locality.

Goal: Implement the "Sustained Batch Fairness Orchestrator" (SBO) — an SLO-aware admission + soft-preemption system that: (1) protects latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) for interactive routes, (2) maintains high GPU utilization by enabling progressive, low-cost preemption for background batches, (3) preserves KV cache hotsets where possible via selective soft-eviction, and (4) exposes controls for Dedicated/Private customers to tune fairness vs cost.

Design highlights:
- Admission controller computes per-request "latency headroom" and assigns a dynamic weight based on SLA class and recent tail-latency trend.
- Batch scoring: each inflight batch receives a GPU Memory Impact score + KV pressure score (hotset overlap, estimated working set) and a progress fraction.
- Soft preemption: rather than immediate termination, we allow yielding at token boundaries with backoff windows. The scheduler issues a Yield request that (a) flushes partial outputs to client when supported, (b) checkpoints KV slab hints, and (c) migrates resumable work to low-priority GPU slot if available.
- KV cache policy: introduce "pin tokens" for active interactive sessions to reduce cold-start regression; background jobs are allowed opportunistic eviction with an LRU/heat hybrid and priority buckets. Eviction decisions favor minimizing regression (based on historical cache miss cost model) rather than pure recency.
- Memory scoring & reclamation: combine CUDA allocation introspection with model trace estimates to compute a reclaim cost. When memory pressure crosses thresholds, the SBO issues graded reclamation requests (soft yield -> partial KV eviction -> full preempt).
- Fairness model: proportional shares by SLA class with a smoothing window (exponential decay) to prevent noisy short bursts from permanently disadvantaging tenants. We provide a tunable fairness knob (alpha) surfaced in Console.

Metrics to track: p50/p95/p99 by SLA class, batch throughput (tokens/s), GPU utilization, KV hit rate, preemption count/type (soft/partial/full), cost delta (tokens/opportunity), user-visible resumed request latency. Success criteria: maintain p95 SLOs within 5% of baseline for interactive routes while improving GPU utilization >=5% vs today and keeping KV-regression alerts rare (<3/day on a cluster).

Trade-offs & risks:
- Soft yield increases system complexity and requires client compatibility for resumable outputs; fallback to harsh preempt if clients don't support streaming/checkpointing.
- Aggressive KV eviction reduces cold-start tail but may lower quality for resumed generations; mitigation via history-based cost model.
- Smoothing window introduces slower responsiveness to sudden tenant behavior changes; we add emergency preemption gate for severe overloads.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype admission scoring and memory/kv cost model in staging (2 weeks).
2) Add soft-yield control path and client-side minimal resume API spec (Confluence + SDK PR) (3 weeks).
3) Implement KV priority buckets and hybrid eviction (2 weeks).
4) End-to-end tests, chaos injection (OOM, network flaps) and perf benchmarking on dedicated nodes (2 weeks).
5) Canary rollout on low-volume region with telemetry and rollback hooks (1 week).

Artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Sustained+Batch+Fairness+Orchestrator, SDK resume API spec: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XG-sbo-sdk-spec, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2839, perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/sbo-batching-dashboard

Rollout & observability: We'll add per-tenant preemption_reason tags, a sampling trace for yield/resume cycles, and a Console surface for fairness alpha and current KV pressure. Canary will run against a mirrored workload for 48 hours and require no more than 2 regression alerts to proceed to wider rollout.

2026-02-25 - Review (PM): Lina Torres: Good direction; ensure console knobs are gated by enterprise plan. Add a customer-impact assessment entry to the ticket.

2026-03-03 - Marcus: Implemented soft-yield handshake on SDK (minimal resume token). Raised PR #2839. Need integration tests for clients that don't support resume: fallback should use immediate preempt and retry via lower-priority queue.

2026-03-08 - Eng Feedback (Ben K.): Memory scoring needs to include fragmentation estimate from allocator; otherwise reclaim cost underestimates in long-lived containers. Added dependency to allocator introspection task.

2026-03-12 - Marcus: Canary on us-west-2 started (node-pool-beta). Early signals: p95 for interactive routes within 3% of baseline; KV miss spike observed on two tenants — tuning eviction heat threshold for background buckets this week.
